messages.content: It's so dark. But she has never seen light. It's so tight. But she has never felt the open air. She can't breathe. But she has never needed to take a breath. All that exists is the rhythmic beating in the walls, comfortably cradling her body. It is all she has ever known.
Everything around her felt so weird. An experience you have gone through but can't remember only re-experienced through dreams.
Suddenly, pressure. A pushing, pulsating force, directing her tiny body. She's not able to resist the flow.
A small panic sets in as the flow takes her

Light. Blinding. Breath. Filling her lungs. It's a sudden, sharp transition. Overwhelming. As her body adjusts, something takes hold of her. A giant looming figure. In place of the all-encompassing walls, a gentle hand moves her body. Then, she sees it. A woman's face. Cutting through everything is an exhausted, pained expression. She doesn't know what it is. Who it is. But there's love behind it.
Briar can't help but smile watching the scene. That look of love something she always wished for

She can't smile. She can't move at all. Something is wrong. Something is terribly, terribly wrong. Her little lungs feel tight. She's stopped taking in air. Confusion sets in on the face in front of her, followed by panic.
She wants to move, understand what's going, what went wrong?
Just as suddenly as she was brought into this space, she's taken away. Another small, enclosed space. Warm air envelops her, but she feels so cold.
The sensation is confusing, she wants to open her eyes to see around her.
Does she want to live?
She does, more than anything.
She shouted her wish at the heart of the world.
And the world answered.
Warmth drains from her surroundings, filling every inch of her body. A beautiful, otherworldly sensation. The girl refuses to die, and thus lives with as much strength as she can.
Feelings of determination and satisfaction take over her mind. She will live no matter what

Time passes. It's only a few days later. She's a healthy, happy little thing. It's as if she had never faced any complications in the first place. A small boy holds her in his arms, only a few years older than her.
She smiles at him waving one of her little arms around.

He notices, and returns the smile. After wrapping her securely in a blanket, he begins to carry her around their house. He stops at the end of a hall, and peeks around its corner. A man and a woman sit across from one another. They appear stressed.
She stretches out her arm opening and closing her hand in their direction, wondering why aren't they smiling too.

The sounds of their voices reach her. She can't glean any information from them. It's only later in her life that the meaning of their words could be understood. By then, she will have forgotten she ever witnessed this. It is a contradiction, only resolvable in a liminal space within her subconscious.

The man is the first to speak. "There's... no evidence the events are linked. Stranger things have happened."
Her little head turns towards the small boy wondering if he knows what the conversation is referring to

The boy seems confused, but intrigued. He waits, and listens.

"Don't give me that!" The woman snaps back at the man. Her voice wavers as she speaks. "You... you know what this is. You know what happened then. Why it happened. Don't... don't lie to yourself for my sake. It's my fault, it has to be. Because... because..."
Her smile disappears, she cries stretching her arms towards the woman's direction.

The boy seems to panic for a moment, and quickly places a hand over her mouth. Whatever this is, he doesn't want it interrupted. They have to see this.

The man's shoulders slump down. His expression grows grim as he witnesses the woman on the verge of tears. He responds slowly. "I know it seems farfetched, after what the doctor told us. I'll never forget that moment, thinking our little girl could never make it. But... she did. We have to focus on that. Whatever else happened... it's a coincidence."
She quiets down and moves her small hand to grab a part of his hand.

Her touch seems to relax the boy. He releases her mouth, instead holding her hand between his fingers.

"That's not true! It's because I... I..." The woman holds her head in her hands, inconsolable. "I wished for more than I was capable of. It was an impossible dream. We... we already had complications with Theo. One child was all I could ever manage. But... I didn't want him to be alone. So I reached too high. Then... worse than failing... I couldn't accept my failure. I cried and screamed for help. For someone to save my baby. I know what happened then... It's the only explanation... I must have made a deal with the reaper! They saved her... but the price was too high! How else can you explain her miraculous recovery!? How else can you explain what happened to that other... th-the other... that poor child... w-was it just because she was the closest...? I had no right... I had no right..."
Her hand tightens, she wishes she could hug her. That she could make her smile.

"..." The man's expression falls. He doesn't reach over to the woman. He sits in an uncomfortable silence. Only breaking it once. "...I know. I'm sorry... I know."

The boy looks worried, processing all that he's heard. He silently creeps back in the direction he came from. Then, he takes several loud steps down the hall, as if it were the first time he had entered into earshot of the couple's conversation. They spot him as he rounds the corner, and attempt to clean up their expressions.
Briar's arm stretches out towards the woman closing and opening her hand like before

The woman turns to the boy. Then, her eyes turn to his hands. To what he is holding. Her eyes see the boy. Her eyes see the blanket. Then, they seem to glaze over, passing over what is contained within the blanket. Briar's eyes are not met with her mothers. They never will be again.
Her arm slowly goes back down, feeling the rejection in her small heart

The boy retreats, holding his sister tightly. He runs back to his room, and slumps down against the wall. Holding his sister out, he meets her eyes, with an intensity in his own.

"Briar..."
Her big eyes stare at him back and she cant help but begin to cry

He holds her close to his chest. "I know... I know. Briar... no, sis... if... if they won't look at you... then I will. I'll never stop looking at you. I promise. So don't cry... Kit's here for you. I'm always gonna be."
She cries and cries stretching her arms at him asking for comfort

He embraces her. He tries his very best. He tries to grant her the warmth she needed. It was an impossible goal. An impossible dream. That he could ever give her what she was missing. The unconditional love that should be granted to a child by a parent. Still, he tried.

Was it enough?
**End Chapter 10.4**

A young Calamari eats her dinner at the family dining table. Her father, Emil, sits across from her. A plate is prepared for her mother, Pearl, but she hasn't arrived home yet.

At this point in time, Pearl still maintains a modicum of a parental attitude. She's attempted to keep her arguments away from Calamari, for the most part.
I take a stab at my spaghetti. As I'm still chewing, I look up at my dad and smile, noodles hanging grossly between my teeth. "Thanks for the food, pops!"
He doesn't seem to mind the disgusting sight. He just smiles and nods. "It's no problem at all, Lammy."
I roll my eyes, clearly not getting the reaction I wanted. The pasta is pretty good, though. A little on the bland side, but I suppose that's what the cheese is for.
I swallow. "Any plans tonight? You wanna come on my walk with me?"
He thinks this over. "Sorry, I might have to sit this one out. I wouldn't want you mother to arrive to an empty house."

"Oh, come onnn... we used to do it all the time! She's not going to yell at you any less just because you're stuck in place like a fucking scarecrow." My tone of voice dips weirdly on the swear, not used to doing it around my family.
He raises an eyebrow, but doesn't comment on the swear. "I'm... not attempting to avoid angering her. I want to be here in case she needs me. It's the least I can do, considering what I can't do."
"Yeah? And what exactly can't you do that you *were* doing before?"
"Ah, no... I really shouldn't be discussing that. The details would bore you, anyway." He stands from the table. "Why don't we go on that walk?"
I stay sitting. "We haven't finished eating, dad."
"Maybe you haven't, but I'm full. Tell you what, I'll be waiting outside." He motions to the front door.
I point at his plate. "Why did you give yourself more than you wanted?"
"Whatever..." I get up too. I was thinking about keeping him here to talk about the 'details', but I just realized that I can ask him about those while we're walking. Duh.
He smiles, as if he's won the interaction. After putting on a jacket, he exits through the door.
I follow, not putting on a jacket. If it's cold outside, I'll suffer like I'm meant to.
It's fairly chilly. As they leave the house, Emil broaches a new conversation topic. "So, how are things with the Acilis boy? Sounds like you two have been getting along well, hm?"

"We've always gotten along well, dad. He lives right next to us. We can go knock on his door, if you want. I mean, I don't want to do that, he's probably eating or something. Since usually it takes longer than two seconds to finish dinner. Y'know. Unless you're being weird."
"That's a good call. Best not to bother a neighbor this late. Good head on your shoulders, that'll come in handy. I trust you've been doing well in your studies?"
"I've been doing great! You know that!" I give an exasperated sigh. "Can we please just talk about the *details* now? You're not going to make me stop thinking about it..."
"What if I already have, and you just haven't noticed it?" He taps his forehead.
"What?!" I think about it really hard.
"Wait, do you have dementia?" This is said with genuine concern.
"No, no, I've got my head screwed on tight. You worry about yourself, alright?"

"Why are you making fun of me??" I stop walking. "What the bell, dad? Can we just have a real talk, instead of you making everything a joke? I'm worried now! You made me worried! I don't like being worried about you!"

He stops ahead of her, and turns around. "Lammy... it's not your job to be concerned about your parents. I've never wanted to burden you with that. I'm not trying to make fun of you, I just... I think you should be acting your age, you know? Thinking about boys, and school."
"Ew! I don't even have any boys I want to think about! You're being gross now!" I stick out my tongue.
"What's the point of a father, if not to embarrass his kid?" He smiles in amusement. "You know, sometimes you remind me so much of your mother."
"Well, I wouldn't leave you behind to eat dinner on your own."
"She's... been having a tough time, recently." He closes his eyes, and lets out a deep sigh. "Promise you won't mention that I told you the details?"
"I literally could not mention that because you didn't."
"I meant after I tell you about them. Which I'm going to do now. If you promise that."
"Oh!"
"Okay. Yeah, I promise. I won't do that. I wouldn't do it anyways."

"Your mother's gotten fired from... a lot of gigs recently. Some big, some small. I... keep trying to get her roles. Get her on stage, to perform... even if it's not as a star. But she's... difficult to work with. The managers find it easier to replace her, than to deal with her, ah, creative differences. They've told me I need to stop pushing for her. I could lose my job. She didn't take it well when I let her know."
"Maybe she should try practicing more. Did you tell her that?"

"It's not a matter of talent." He pauses. "Not just a matter of talent. Regardless, she's been told that plenty of times, but she already thinks she's the best around. It's... well, I don't want to say impossible, but... a monumental task to change her mind."
"Isn't that what the point of a husband is?"
"Some people might argue that, but I've never been a fan of the notion." He stares into the sky. The stars are visible, shining in the night sky. "Do you know why I fell in love with your mother?"
I start walking again. "Because she used to be pretty, and her voice used to be good, and she used to be nice to you."

"Who said she isn't pretty anymore?" He walks to her side. "She's gotten... more brash recently. But she's never exactly been kind. She's always been headstrong. Difficult to work with. Argumentative. And so sure that she's in the right."
"Wait, were you being mean to me when you said I was like her?"
"I'm not argumentative! I don't argue that much!"
"I like agreeing with people!"

"...I like agreeing with people, too. It's one of the things I'm best at. It's how I got to where I am. I can keep a whole room of board members pacified. It's easy, once you get what makes them tick. But, Lammy... you don't have to be agreeable."
"I know that. I'm not saying I *always* go along with what people tell me to do. Honestly, I think you're just trying to give advice to yourself. You don't always have to agree with people, dad."
"You don't always have to agree with mom."
"No... I'm where I want to be." He places his hands behind his head. "I haven't told you why I fell in love yet."
I sigh. "Go ahead and tell me, then."

"Your mother lives her life unapologetically. She doesn't overthink her actions. She doesn't account for those around her. She sees her goals, and she runs for them, without compromise. I think that's the most beautiful thing in this world. Everyone has their own life, their own rules, their own way of living. But not everyone lives that life to the fullest. They'll suppress parts of themselves, through shame and doubt. I think I was just waiting, my whole life, to find someone so confident, that they could ignore everyone else's rules. That's how I live my life to the fullest, by keeping my eyes on her..." He turns to face Calamari. "...and on you. Like I said, you remind me so much of her. No one can decide who are you are, other than you. If there's one thing you never let change about yourself, that should be it."
I scoff, suddenly weirdly uncomfortable. "Yeah. Thanks, dad. Good to know."

I didn't decide who I am. There was never a day I woke up and thought, wow, I'm really feeling Calamari! Nobody does that. Nobody's a blank slate. Definitely not me. I've been me as long as I can remember, and I guarantee mom has too. She just likes to pretend that it isn't true. That's what he's saying he likes about her, that she claimed ownership over something that didn't belong to her. That she's a thief, getting mad about her stolen goods not being valuable anymore. He's an idiot. He's an idiot! Stupid.
"I really do wish you would look away sometimes, though."

"Half of our spaghetti went to waste! It's just sitting on her plate back home. I care a lot about the spaghetti, dad. It's too good... you got me addicted... I'm a deranged pasta freak..." I swipe at his arm.
He deftly dodges the swipe. "Well, now I've found something I don't want to keep my eyes on. No one wants to see a deranged pasta freak."
"Grahhhh... stay on your toes, pasta man. If your skin got any lighter, it might start looking suspiciously like dough."
I don't really like the bit I'm doing. It feels desperate, somehow. But I didn't want to keep talking about mom.

He never actually told me what he couldn't do, did he? Was it just not being able to get her jobs? Or does he think he's missing something else, too? I don't know. I don't really want to know anymore. I feel too bad to ask a third time.
I swipe at him again, but keep walking.
That was a pretty revolting memory, all things considered. One can only hope it will be the last.
**End Chapter 10.4**

The world reforms. In one direction, an endless expanse of water extends beyond the horizon. In the opposite direction, an endless expanse of sand. The line in which they meet travels down the remaining two. Nearby, the man in white robes stares towards the ocean, his hair flowing in the cool breeze.
Atie looks at him, unsure of anything.
He meets her eyes. It's just for a moment, before he turns back to the water. "I figured you needed a break. That was pretty intense. Running straight into your friend after that... bad luck."
"Do you control it?"
"Just these... 'dreams'. If you wish to think of them that way. Out there, I'm chained. To your friends, it won't seem as if any time passed."
"So... when you decide to end this... will I be left back where I was, with Val? Or was that not the 'out there'?"
"...What an astute question." He sits down on the sand. The waves lap at his feet. "It's all layered. There's always been an 'out there' no matter where you are."
"Why?"

"Each layer down is made in the image of the one above. Symbols are cast like shadows in the intersection, losing a dimension in the process. The imaginary made real. It's hard to say why these layers keep getting made. Greed, discontent, curiosity. We're just left to pick up the pieces, staring out at our glass cage."
"Has it always been this way?"

"Sorry to disappoint, but I haven't always been around to watch. Or, if I was, then I can't recall." As the waves reach further inland, he cups some water in his hands. "...There's a lot I've never seen, even in this world. Newark is a coastal country, right? Have you ever seen the ocean?"
"I think I have..."

"Well, I haven't. This is my best approximation. I'm sure it doesn't live up to the real sight." The water slips through his fingers. "It's not based on nothing. I haven't seen it, but I've felt it. There used to be so much more of it. Why do you think that is? Did the water go somewhere... or did more land come from somewhere?"
"More of it...? Huh...?"

"...I can't explain it either. Before this week, I hadn't spoken to someone in so long. All I have is my observations. I lack the ability to go out and find the answers." He lays down in the sand, closing his eyes. "Maybe that's why I feel so calm. I'm so close now. Soon, I'll be able to see everything hidden from me."
"How so? And... um... what really are you?"

"I'm every grain of sand beneath your feet. I'm every brick Paradise is built from. I'm the plants grown between cracks. I'm the bodies buried beneath unmarked graves." The tide begins to recede. "I used to be so small. A single, fragile body. I've grown so much since then. I can feel this entire town. I course through its veins."
"I cannot grasp what that means..."

"Think of it like vines grown from a single seed. That seed is my original body. Locked away. Immobile. But something has grown out of me. My core isn't large enough, or strong enough to hold what I feel. So my soul has wrapped itself around this town." The air feels dry. The sun is beating down a blazing hot fury. "That's what broke that machine, your prime minister. He was plugged into me, and couldn't handle even a fraction of my rage. It will boil over, and shatter my cage. Only then will I be free to see the world outside."

The air suddenly cools, and the water returns gently. "But that doesn't really have anything to do with you. Are you ready to go back?"
"Do I have a choice?"
"Sure. You can stay here and watch the ocean with me, if you want. I'm not in any hurry to get you out of here. Like I said, no time is really passing right now."
"Then I will stay longer."
He doesn't say anything in response. He just smiles, feeling the warmth of the sun, and the cool ocean breeze.
((End session))
The waves ebb and flow, in accordance to the tide. There is nothing to wait for. Here, this is all that will be. Despite that knowledge, there is still a certain allure.

Atie watches the waves. Someone more attached to the ocean would likely be able to pick apart what has been reconstructed incorrectly. This ocean may not even serve its purpose to them.
To Atie, it seems... fine. She doesn't need any more than that, or at least, she has never known a need for it. She knows she should be soothed by their movement, so she tries to be. Not how much, or why.
Fake, incorrect waves, presented for the enjoyment of people who don't actually care about them, in order to give the surface-level appearance of a calming moment in a beach. Atie smirks, wondering what the point even is, before turning to the man and continuing to talk.
"What's your name?"

The waves fill the silence, as he considers this question. "I was never given one. I didn't belong to my parents. I don't even remember them. Instead, I belonged to my role. A servant. To people, then to faith. Someone like that doesn't need a name. Just a title. Boy. Child. Man. All in white."
"What do you do here?"

"I haven't done anything in a long time. Not here. Not anywhere. Once, I was the personal servant to the heir of Paradise. Then, I was a volunteer under the church of Panthium. Now, all I can do is wait."
"You just pulled me out of reality, and created this scene. It's not just waiting."
"It... depends on how you look at it. If it doesn't have an effect out there, I'm not really sure it can be called doing anything at all."
"If I still remember this when I go back, that's an effect."
"I suppose there is some comfort in that. Still, I don't think it will change what you will do, or what happens to you. And... It could never satiate my rage."
"What is this rage about?"

"Isn't it the most natural thing in the world? A caged animal, lashing out. I don't seek revenge, or to change the world that trapped me. I just want to hurt something. Whatever's in front of me. I want it to feel what I feel."
"Will you hurt me?"
"I think... it would be best if you left town. When you can."
"Does that mean no?"
"I cannot hurt you right now. This place, and my form here... they don't really exist. But when I can... if you are still in this town... I am going to kill you. I will not hesitate."
"But what for? Will it help set you free, or change your life?"
"Of course not. Don't try to understand it. There's no greater goal. It's not even a desire, really. I don't have enough left for that."
"If not understand, what can I do for you, then?"
"Why would you want to do something for me? I don't need anything from you. I will free myself. I will feel my rage. That's all I need."
"Didn't you say it won't help set you free?"
"That's because my freedom is a prerequisite. How could I hurt anyone from within this cage?"
"But is being free not what you want?"
"Wants are an illusion. I've been around long enough to realize that. Childish fantasies. My freedom... my rage... it's all just instinct. It's simply in my nature."
"If you say so."

"That's why... you confused me so much, at first. You want to create something. You want to make the world better, through modifications to the natural order. It was strange, and I didn't understand. I still don't think I do... but that's not so bad. I hope you succeed, in whatever form that takes."
"Thanks. I bet you'd enjoy it too, if you allowed yourself to."
"...I think it's time for you to go. I'm not used to such extended company. It's not bad, but... I'm tired."

Atie smiles.
"That's familiar. I understand."
"Goodbye, Atie Alcule. For now, or forever. It's up to you." The man in white disappears from sight, as the beach and the waves gently fade away.
**End Prologue**

The world reforms. The boy, now grown into a young man, sweeps the floor of the church. Draped in white robes, he stands tall, silken hair flowing behind him. His eyes, locked on his task, are subtly different than before. Their deep, amber contents have begun to swirl beneath the surface, just barely.
She grabs her right hand with her left, and presses the nail of her left thumb into her right palm.
She feels pressure on her palm. She feels pain if she presses hard enough.
*What am I doing...?*
She walks forward, towards the boy.
He stops sweeping upon noticing her approach. "Oh, greetings. Is there something I can assist with? Once I have finished the task assigned to me by the Father, of course."
She moves to speak, but feels she cannot. The words elude her. Rather than speak what she wants, she moves to something else.
"How have things been for you here, child?"
"I have been well. I appreciate the hospitality that I have been shown. I owe much to the church, and to the Father especially. Is there a reason for your concern?"
"Your leg. How is it now?"
"It was a miracle. The Prince witnessed my plight, and granted me his blessing." He stands on one leg to demonstrate the point.
Alonsa doesn't respond.
Returning to a normal stance, he looks over her, slightly confused. "...Was there anything else?"
She sighs.
She moves to the side of the room, and takes a seat.
"You've grown a lot."
"I know you've never considered me like the Father. I've never been... there for you in the same ways. I am not asking you to, of course."
"I just worry sometimes that you think I do not care for you."

He looks to the side. "That... that would be an inappropriate thought for me to carry. I am aware of how much this church works to assist the town, and I am included in that. It takes a great kindness to offer such devotion."
“We all have our responsibilities to the church… but we also have responsibilities to eachother. In a sense, they’re one and the same.”
“To do one without the other is purposeless.”
He gives an awkward smile. "I'm... not quite sure I understand. If they are one and the same, how can I do one without the other? By assisting the church, I do help others."
“I speak of myself, not you.”
“You’ve been so helpful these last few years. I fear sometimes that my appreciation for that isn’t communicated.”
"Ah, well... I find fulfillment in the work itself, but your words are still appreciated. Thank you for taking the time to speak so candidly."
“Of course…”
There’s more to say, but she can’t find the words for them.

The boy returns to his task. With a sweep of the broom, sand is kicked up into the air. It begins to swirl around the room, reforming it before her eyes. Time passes. The boy is seated, covered in bruises. The Father stands above him, with a furious expression.
Alonsa watches from afar.

"I cannot believe you would be so *foolish*. After everything we have done for you." The Father speaks through gritted teeth. "How did you receive these? What thrill were you seeking in the night, when I was unable to protect you? Raiding a camp? Wrestling a wild beast?"

The boy looks ashamed, casting his eyes anywhere other than the Father.
“Father, don’t be so harsh.”

The Father shakes his head. "These actions cannot be allowed. He must understand. These reckless, irresponsible actions not only endanger himself, but damage our church. How can he act as an extension of the Prince's will, with his form tarnished so?"
She is silent, but extends an empathetic glance at the boy.

"He must be taught. How to elevate himself above such childish, masculine impulses. It is a flaw, coded into his blood, that must be expunged. How else can he hope to maintain his beauty?" The Father lifts the boy's chin, forcing him to meet his eyes.
A flaw, coded into blood? Can such a thing exist?
"Father, he made a mistake. He won't do it again."

"I find that difficult to believe. My child, how many times have I cured your injuries? How many times have you ran right back? How many more times will I need to fix you?"

The Boy speaks nervously. "I... do have a concern about that, Father. I think it may be best if we... let these bruises heal naturally."
She looks inquisitively at the boy.

"It's... becoming more difficult to use my body. Those areas healed by miracles... each time, they feel less... themselves. Sometimes, it is as if I feel something moving beneath my skin." The boy grips onto his formerly broken leg.
“Why do you put yourself in these situations, child? Healing magic can have long-term effects on repeated use…”

He doesn't answer, just gripping himself tighter.

The Father contemplates this for a moment. "Questioning the blessing of the Prince is already bordering on blasphemy. However, if you have reservations... then we simply must ensure you cease this foolishness."
"Father, what does that mean...?"

The sands are lifted in the current once again. The room reforms into the underground catacombs. Deep in the heart of the labyrinthine tunnels, The Father stands over the boy. The boy's arms and legs have been restrained by metal cuffs, chained to the sandstone walls.
"Father..."

"It is a temporary measure. It must be done, for his own good. Until he has learned to behave with the grace befitting of his role." The Father speaks harshly. All the while, the boy stares up at him, as something begins to pack itself tightly behind his eyes.
"Father, please. You shouldn't... this isn't... you can't do this to him."

"The decision has been made. We have given him freedom, and it only resulted in his suffering. Is his protection, the safety of his skin, not worth more than anything? What are we here for, if not to help him grow into a Prince of his own?"
"Suffering for who? Him, who will strive for freedom no matter what we do, or us, who take his suffering as our own responsibilities?"
"This cannot be the right thing to do. This cannot be what the Prince would want."

"Do you believe the Prince wished for his own imprisonment? Did the Hero ask his permission, or was it simply what had to be done? To protect him from his cursed blood, and from the Reaper's clutches. We will play this role, follow the Hero's teachings, and help this child ascend into what he was meant to be."
"What he is meant to be??"
"He is a human being, Father. No one is meant to be anything other then what they are. To claim so would go against the teachings of this very church!"
"Don't allow your anger to get in the way of this..."

"I see. I understand now where your confusion is sourced from. I am not punishing my child in anger. I am protecting him, out of my love." He approaches Alonsa, placing his arms against the wall, trapping her between them. "As far as I can see, the only thing getting in the way is you. Not anymore. You shall be the first to listen to the song of the Prince."
"What?"

The Father hums a melody. A simple tune. Quietly, yet firmly, he speaks. "Sing for us, my child. Sing for me."

The boy shuts his eyes, and lowers his head. He repeats the tune, vocalizing the song that has been requested of him. His voice carries throughout the room, echoing off the walls, and centering itself on Alonsa and the Father. She feels her body go numb, her senses dulling. She's conscious, but she cannot hold herself up, as if her bones have turned to jelly.
She tries to scream.

Nothing comes out. Even if it did, her mouth soon begins to melt, her entire body softening. She and the Father collapse onto one another. His body seems to be under the same adverse effects. Their flesh mingles with one another, suffusing into one form.
She tries to reach out to the boy.

Her arm is no longer her own. Her will is overpowered. Her body leans further into the embrace, the joining of two forms, without questioning its new host. The Father's body pulls itself together, while pulling her body into his own. 

Her flesh is rearranged, her organs and muscles remade to fit new roles. To allow room for such an addition, his body must contort into a horrible form. His head separates from his collar, further and further stretching out the skin between. The space is filled with her flesh, reinforced by her bones. A needle and thread. Your hands are clumsy. You stab yourself more than once. Your body is no longer the same. Your arms feel gangly. Your fingers feel twisted. You sew up your torn robes. A new shape. One that will fit your new form.
I move each finger individually, and try to get a sense of having more joints.

As your fingers move, your other hand grabs them, holding them steady. Your mouth moves. It speaks words aloud. "Side effects. Muscle spasms? The process was messy. Rushed. I was left no choice. Unfortunate."
I attempt to speak.
Your attempt is a failure.
My lip quivers, but no words come out. I can feel my throat refusing to move at my command, my body losing control.

Your hands move to finish repairing your robes. Patchwork, with uneven spacing. Whole, but not congruent. You cover yourself. Your form. It is too much for the townsfolk. They would not understand. You look in the mirror. Something must be done. Your face has been rearranged. Nose and mouth, misplaced. Your eyes, separate from your eyelids. They can no longer be shut.

Despite my faithfulness, I have always questioned the relationship between the body and the soul. Our faith teaches us that upon our deaths, the souls of the righteous shall be transported to a place of higher nobility. However, when we envision these souls, we see them as simply ourselves, taking on the form of our bodies. To me, this always incidated that the very construct of an identity, a soul, was inherently linked to our bodies. Our self perception stems from the form we inhabit, and if a soul truly does exist independently of the body, the shape of the soul is determined by the physical qualities of the creature
With that in mind, what shall become of my soul? A soul who’s mold has been melted into wax, who’s meat and bones have been digested and integrated into another?

Perhaps it means I died, when I was consumed, and all that’s left is the lingering, twitching thoughts of a ghostless vessel. Or maybe my soul, too, was absorbed into the greater creature, no longer mine at all.
I wonder if I can die anymore.

You stare at the boy. The man. The child. He rattles his chains in fury and desperation. Eventually, he pulls hard enough to break. The metal chains do not fracture. A bone protrudes roughly from his arm. He screams.
I wince.

You forge a mask; your visage is to be hidden. Upon your face, an illusion is born. Combined with the silhouette granted by the robe, an impression of a unified being is born. All that has been added is extra meat. In the cover of the night, you abscond from your tower. There is business to attend to.
My body gets to work, my being moves with it.

The town changes through the years. It must not be allowed. When the boy is to return, all will be as it was. It is what forged him. What allowed, not for the birth of his form, but the birth of his self. It must not be lost. It must not be tarnished. It must be tamed, like a wild beast. Under your instruction, the boy's song carries through the town. The people's skin is left soft and young. The wear and tear in the buildings recede. Nothing is to age. Nothing is to be built.
How long has it been?

The boy's skin reseals itself. His bone retracts into his body. It's not the same. It's not his shape. There is no mold to be used.

Years turn to decades. The appearance can be changed, reverted, but the flesh will still age. Then, it will rot. Soon, the town will be dead. Something must be done. You must preserve this until he has learned.
I suppose, it’s what I’ve always done.
In that sense, nothing has changed.

A solution. You've found it. If flesh will age, it must only be replaced. When a cycle has reached its end, children are born. Grown. Aged into adults. They are ready to be used. New vessels. One by one. The original is melted, unformed. All except for the mind, to be poured into a new body. The opposite procedure, for the recipient. Memories ripped away, and discarded. Identities kept. Indistinguishable. Memories are fuzzy. An acceptable consequence. Helpful, even. Keeps the town dwellers deaf to the process.
It’s what I’ve always done. It’s what… we’ve always done.

The boy grows more desperate. If fractured limbs will not free him, then he begins to break more. He slams his head on the cold, hard sandstone. His skull fractures open. Flesh oozes out from within. He is not deterred. Again. Again. And again. He breaks and breaks and breaks.

Leftovers. Twins. More children than needed. The population has been refreshed. What is to be done with the extras. You must find a place for them.

Of course. He will be used as your own. Meat for yourself. The boy's body is immortal; he does not seem to age, even as he distorts. You, on the other hand, seem to have only slowed the process. Your throat stretches, making room for the new addition.
The day I became meat, I lost my sense of time. I feel as if I perceive every moment of my existence simultaneously. How long has it been? Ten centuries or ten seconds, it’s all the same.

The boy's head seals itself. He is once again contained within his own skin. His face is unrecognizable, if it can even be called a face. It is a tragedy. You wonder why he does not stop. Why he continues to hurt himself, even now. Why does he not love himself as you do.

Outsiders arrive in the town. They are poking their noses around. It is a problem. It could lead to a bigger problem. You are a man of peace. You will not tarnish your own soul. Your own hands, which were meant to guide your Prince. A deal must be struck.
Poor, poor child.
Worry not, we shall serve as your guardians evermore.

You approach the mayor of the town. You know what she wants. It is frustrating, but possible. You grant her a child. A child allowed to grow outside the cycle you have created. She's right, to be afraid of us.

The boy breaks, and breaks, and breaks. Every piece of his body that could be broken, has been broken. His arms, then his hands, then his fingers, then his knuckles. Before your eyes, he changes ever so slowly. Years to decades to centuries to millennia. Can you even remember what he used to be. There is only one saving grace. The pain the child endures is the pain of the citizens. The wounds inflicted onto him are the wounds inflicted upon us by the Reaper itself. Rejoice, child. You are the greatest sin-eater to have ever existed. With you, we shall ascend to the highest heights of heaven.

A mound of flesh sits before you. Gravity weighs it down, sinking its bottom wider than its top. Were that not the case, it may appear as a perfect sphere. A smooth, uniform skin stretches across it. Inside, its flesh has homogenized. It is incapable of harming itself. It will no longer be broken.

You shut a large double door, sealing it away. It is safe from itself, but an outsider could still bring it harm. It must be protected. Extra security measures are taken. Four keys, to be scattered. Hidden. You have decided on locations for three. You take the fourth into your hand. What is to be done with it?
I place a small rope through the hole at the top, and tie it around my neck. I keep it with me at all times.
So it is. So it always was.
